neighbours.label: the last piece of a rare proper name split into several tokens, typically a river or place name before 'River' or 'County' (Truck|ee, Desch|utes), as against names that are a single token
fire: Salmon still spawn in the Willamette River near Portland.
Orchards line the Okanogan River for many miles.
The bridge spans the Susquehanna River at Harrisburg.
Rafters run the Tuolumne River in early summer.
Mills once crowded the banks of the Merrimack River.
Fog settles over the Shenandoah River most mornings.
A pipeline spill fouled the Kalamazoo River in 2010.
In 1969 the Cuyahoga River famously caught fire.
quiet: Salmon still spawn in the Columbia River near Portland.
Orchards line the Hudson River for many miles.
The bridge spans the Missouri River at Bismarck.
Rafters run the Colorado River in early summer.
Mills once crowded the banks of the Ohio River.
Fog settles over the Thames River most mornings.
A pipeline spill fouled the Mississippi River in 2010.
In 1969 the Amazon River flooded much of the basin.
